x: We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.

Congratulations must also go to George Checkley, who, after his disappointing disqualification in the R.W.A. National 10, travelled to Eastleigh a few days later and won the National Police 10 Miles Championship against all the usual London opposition.

Unfortunately George Checkley was far from fit and was much further back than he should have been. Don Fotheringham walked well to finish inside the hour and work his way into the third handicap team accompanied by Stan Vickers, Eric Hall and Ted Smith.

Ron West, a second claim member who was walking in the handicap which was held in conjunction, walked an exceptionall good race to beat Eric for first place. George Checkley, rapidly coming back to form was a good second, with Syd James 3rd.

At 5 miles, Eric Hall, George Checkley, Davis of Woodford Green and Bob McMullen led the field with Beecham moving up. Harry was still hanging back, but catching sight of Fred Rolfe and Doub he put on pressure and soon passed them.

W.C. set off at a great pace accompanied by Johnson of Sheffield and Huchison, also Met., and at the first 10 k.metre stage these three were in the lead with Eric Hall and George Checkley lying 5th and 6th respectively, 27 seconds behind the leaders.

George Checkley, our third man to finish, will not regard this as one of his best races. It certainly did not come up to his performances in the Middlesex Championship and our own Club 20 but the long rail journey and change of routine may have upset him.

Both these walkers, together with George Checkley, have been selected to compete in an "Olympic Trial" and three from one club out of a total of 16 from the whole country, seems a very good proportion.

George Checkley walked a very steady race and once in fourth place, he retained this to the end. George Beecham who took it steady at the start, walked well to finish 6th and Bob Newson over the last four miles, passed Norman Guilmant and really got moving to finish 8th.

George Checkley, the holder of the title was out to retain it, but was challenged by Eric Hall, competing in this race for the first time. There was never much between them until the last lap when Eric moved away to a very convincing win in 2hrs. 52m. 22s. with George 2nd in 2.55.58.

We badly needed the assistance of Bob Newson and George Checkley, but in the circumstances, the lads did very well. In the handicap team race we took 2nd place Eric, Norman, George Beecham and Fred Rolfe sharing the prizes.

Names like Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley, and Jack Bidgood remind us of the past years, but now it would seem that George Checkley and Hugh McGreechan have taken on the task of keeping a Belgrave name on the trophy.

Our "A" Team consisting of Eric Hall, Ted Smith and George Checkley by a fine display of walking, won the event with a distance of 8miles, 869 yards, seven yards better than Woodford Green and our "B" Team were 5th with 8 miles 240 yards.
We received invitations for Stan Vickers, Eric Hall and George Checkley out of 15 from the whole country and although Eric and George were more used to 50 kilometres, they both walked a good race.
In the four miles Eric Hall in 2nd place scored 25 points and George Checkley 6th, 21, making our total for that race 46, to put us in the lead.

A team sponsored by the Union of London Walking Clubs visited Belgium on July 15th to compete in an International race over 50 k.metres and included in the team were two of our walkers, Norman Guilmant and George Checkley.

Ably supported by George Checkley, 6th, Hugh McGreechan 10th and Harry Shields 12th, who enjoyed the last eight miles more than any other part of the race, we easily gained team honours with 18 points to Poly's 36 and Essex Beagles 41.

George Checkley however, who seems to relish such conditions, had moved into an early lead in front of our second man Bob Newson, with Norman Guilmant also moving strongly and it looked rosy at halfway.

George Checkley who had started off at a very fast pace, second to Thompson, began to lose ground and when Crawley was reached had dropped back to fourth place, Vic Stone having gone up to 2nd and the Italian Resta 3rd.

With fine efforts from Eric Hall, Ted Smith, George Checkley and Bob Newson, the latter practically killing himself to take Stan over the last couple of laps, we won the team race from Woodford Green.
George Checkley walked really well to win in 40m.12s. with Bob Newson second, Syd James (whom we are pleased to see out again) third and Eric Froude, still improving, fourth.
